title: Onboard atlas-30b v1.1: metadata, performance profiles, and changelog automation
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Add Atlas-30b v1.1 to the model registry with validated metadata, calibrated performance profiles for common GPU shapes, and automated changelog entry generation. This enables Redwood customers to select Atlas-30b v1.1 from the catalog with conservative latency/throughput expectations and automatic release notes generated from perf artifacts.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds canonical metadata for atlas-30b v1.1 including model config, tokenizer fingerprint, and provenance link to vendor model hub.
- Adds performance profiles (p50/p95 latency and throughput estimates) for A100-80GB, A10G, and T4 with quantization compatibility notes.
- Wires perf artifacts into the changelog automation pipeline so onboarding tests produce a drafted release note summarizing perf numbers and supported runtimes.
- Adds a small perf test that runs in CI perf-matrix to validate profile stability on PRs that touch profile or metadata files.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add model metadata JSON (id, architecture, tokenizer, sha256 of weights).
- [x] Add perf_profiles.yaml with shape-specific profiles and recommended batch sizes.
- [x] Add CI job to run quick perf smoke on a small sample (ci/workflows/model_registry.yml).
- [x] Integrate with scripts/registry/update_changelog.py to generate draft release note.
- [x] Add unit+integration tests for registry loader and perf profile parsing.
- [x] Get approvals from perf and registry reviewers.

Why: Prior onboarding of Atlas-30b (v1.0) was manual and lacked automated perf notes. Customers using Dedicated and Private deployments require predictable performance profiles; having them in the registry improves routing, billing estimation, and rollouts. Automating the changelog reduces manual errors and ensures release notes include verified perf metrics.

Rollout and migration notes: The new metadata is additive and does not change existing model identifiers. The registry loader will pick up v1.1 as a separate version; downstream serving will only pick it up after deploy of the registry index which is part of this PR. No runtime migrations required.

Related: Linear ENG-4217 (onboard atlas variants), PM-189 (catalog expansion). See docs/models/atlas.md for end-user guidance.
